Commentary.Commentary: Can the Pakistani bowlers stand up and do the job today? They will be once again up against a very formidable English batting line-up. Let's see how the run chase pans out. Do join us in a short while.

It's a pitch where Pakistan will miss the services of Yasir Shah. Adil Rashid and Moeen bowled brilliantly and there was ample assistance from the track. The spell with the new ball will be of great importance as well.

England bowled superbly up front and never let Pakistan off the hook. Their spinners, in particular, bowled extremely well in the middle overs to not only choke the run flow but also to pick wickets at regular intervals. At one stage, Pakistan were in a serious danger of getting bundled out well inside the allotted overs but the 56-run stand between Imad Wasim and Hasan Ali for the 8th wicket helped them to add some sort of respect to the total.

Quick runs towards the end all thanks to Imad Wasim and Pakistan have managed to post a fighting total on the board. It was yet another disappointing batting show by the visiting team as apart from skipper Azhar Ali at the top, none of the batsmen showed enough stomach for fight. There were plenty of starts but they threw it away eventually.

Leg bye! Off the mark, Pakistan! Full ball on the pads, Aslam tries to run that fine to the leg side but the ball hits his pads. A leg bye is taken.
Pitches it on the pads, Aslam tucks it to mid-wicket.
Hurls it full outside off, it swings away a bit. Aslam off his front foot pushes it to covers.
Willey starts off with a perfect length ball outside off, Aslam looks at it and lets it through to the keeper.
Sami Aslam and Sharjeel Khan will be the two Pakistani openers. David Willey will begin with the bowling proceedings for England. Here we go...
England team changes - Jonny Bairstow, David Willey, Chris Jordon are in for Jos Buttler, Chris Woakes and Mark Wood.
Pakistan team changes - Imad Wasim, Umar Gul, Mohammad Rizwan and Mohammad Irfan are in for Shoaib Malik, Mohammad Amir, Yasir Shah and Wahab Riaz.
TOSS - Pakistan win the toss and elect to bat first!

Last match saw a plenty of records getting tumbled. From Alex Hales' highest individual score for England to the highest ODI team total, we witnessed all. It is going to be a match where we hope Pakistan show some fightback or the winner of this series England will head for another win. Stay tuned for the toss and other updates.

Hello and a warm welcome everyone for the fourth ODI at Headingley, Leeds. England and Pakistan once again will be up against each other and with the series already in the pocket the hosts would look to go for a cleansweep. The Men in Green, on the other hand, will look to bounce back from the disappointment of the last game and get a win under their name. Let's see how the game pans out.
